Hi Jon,

Thanks for writing in, and sorry the brick gave up on you.

Good news first: on the NerdOctaxe and the whole Nerd / Bitaxe family, a unit that suddenly stops powering on is almost always the power supply rather than the miner itself, so you very likely only need a new supply and the miner stays exactly as it is. I have passed this to my colleague who handles parts, with your model noted, and they are picking it up today and will come back to you in this thread with the correct supply and how to get it to you. Nothing you need to do on that side.

Two things worth knowing while you wait. The O. Gamma is a 12V unit and pulls roughly 200W at full tilt, so it needs a 12V supply with real headroom (about 20A or more) and the right connector on the miner end. Please do not run it off a generic low-cost 12V brick that is only just rated for it: under-rated supplies sag under load, and that is the single most common cause of a Nerd miner rebooting, dropping chips or killing the supply a second time. That is why we would rather send you the matched one than have you guess on Amazon.

The other thing: once the new supply is on it, give it a few minutes and watch the screen and the web UI. If it boots, hashes and holds its chip count, you are done. If it still shows nothing at all, or it powers up but reports zero chips or a VREG error, write back and tell me exactly what the screen says plus your firmware version, because that pattern points at the board rather than the supply and I would look at it differently.

If you want a faster second opinion in the meantime, our Discord is at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and JD, our hardware lead, is there as @nullhashrate.

Happy to keep helping once the new supply is in your hands,
Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support
